distinguishing_feature: COPD is associated with a history of heavy smoking and shows fixed airflow obstruction (post-BD FEV1/FVC <0.7); asthma shows reversible obstruction and onset is typically younger with atopic history.
Asthma shows fully reversible obstruction and often has atopy; COPD shows fixed post-BD obstruction predominantly in older smokers.
Acute bronchitis is self-limiting with no episodic wheeze; asthma features recurrent discrete episodes triggered by allergens/exercise with reversible airflow obstruction.
Asthma features recurrent discrete episodes triggered by allergens/exercise with reversible airflow obstruction; acute bronchitis is entirely self-limiting with no episodic wheeze.
ILD shows restrictive spirometry (reduced TLC) with fine bibasal crackles; COPD shows obstructive spirometry and hyperinflation with coarse breath sounds.
COPD is obstructive with hyperinflation; ILD is restrictive with reduced DLCO and fine bibasal crackles — spirometry pattern is key distinguishing feature.
TB has gradual onset with >3 weeks of cough, night sweats, and upper lobe CXR changes; community pneumonia has acute onset with lobar consolidation and responds to standard antibiotics.
Community pneumonia has acute onset with lobar consolidation and responds to standard antibiotics; TB has gradual onset with >3 weeks of cough, night sweats, and upper lobe CXR changes.
Lung cancer rarely causes fever and responds poorly to antibiotics; TB features systemic symptoms (night sweats, weight loss) and AFB positivity on sputum microscopy.
TB is associated with contact history, AFB-positive sputum, and upper lobe infiltrates; lung cancer is associated with smoking/age, hemoptysis, and a discrete mass on CT.
Pleural effusion can be a complication of lung cancer (malignant effusion) but also occurs in heart failure, infection, and liver disease — cytology and LDH/protein ratio differentiate.
Cytology and LDH/protein ratio distinguish generic effusion from lung cancer; effusion can be a complication of lung cancer (malignant effusion) but also occurs in heart failure/infection.
Pneumothorax shows absent breath sounds with hyper-resonance on percussion; pleural effusion shows absent breath sounds with dullness to percussion.
Pleural effusion causes dullness to percussion; pneumothorax causes hyper-resonance — both reduce breath sounds but are distinguished by percussion note and CXR.
COPD has diffuse airflow obstruction without bronchial dilatation; bronchiectasis shows dilated bronchi on HRCT with copious daily sputum production and recurrent infections.
Bronchiectasis shows dilated bronchi on HRCT with copious daily sputum production and recurrent infections; COPD has diffuse airflow obstruction without bronchial dilatation.
Pneumonia features focal consolidation on CXR, high fever >38.5°C, and productive purulent sputum; acute bronchitis shows a clear CXR and milder systemic symptoms.
Acute bronchitis shows a clear CXR and milder systemic symptoms; pneumonia features focal consolidation on CXR, high fever >38.5°C, and productive purulent sputum.
